headline: 3 killed, 20 injured in Tangail bus-truck collision
summary: A head-on collision between a bus and a truck in Tangail's Madhupur upazila last night resulted in three fatalities and over 20 injuries. All victims were passengers of the bus.
details: At least three people were killed and more than 20 others were injured in a head-on collision between a bus and a truck in Tangail's Madhupur upazila last night. All the deceased and injured were passengers on the bus, according to Madhupur Fire Service Team Leader Borhan Ali.
The accident took place around 10:00 PM in the Raktipara area. Upon receiving information, a fire service team promptly arrived at the scene and initiated rescue operations.
Fire service personnel, aided by local residents, rescued the injured and transported them to Madhupur Upazila Health Complex. The identities of the deceased could not be confirmed immediately.

Madhupur Police Station Inspector (Investigation) Anwar Hossain stated that the bodies of the three deceased are being held at the hospital as efforts to identify them continue. Eight of the injured are currently receiving treatment at Madhupur Upazila Health Complex, while several critically injured victims have been transferred to Mymensingh Medical College Hospital and other healthcare facilities for advanced care.

headline_marked: [[DSCC unveils Tk 4,004 crore budget for FY2026-27]], but past implementation raises questions
headline: DSCC unveils Tk 4,004 crore budget for FY2026-27, but past implementation raises questions
summary: Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) has announced a Tk 4,004 crore budget for the upcoming fiscal year. However, concerns persist regarding its feasibility, as previous budgets saw only about 33% actual expenditure.
details: Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) has announced a budget of Tk 4,004.60 crore for the 2026-27 fiscal year. This represents an increase of approximately Tk 866 crore compared to the revised budget of Tk 3,138.77 crore from the previous fiscal year.

Despite the larger budget, questions are being raised about its full implementation, given the corporation's past performance. Experience from previous years indicates that the entire allocated amount is rarely spent.

The current budget includes Tk 730.93 crore unspent from the previous fiscal year, meaning this amount will not be newly generated income. Furthermore, Tk 540.50 crore is projected to remain unspent by the end of the current fiscal year, suggesting that not all of the announced Tk 4,004 crore is planned for direct citizen services and development work.

The budget was approved on July 26 at a DSCC management committee meeting and announced by Administrator Md Abdus Salam. He stated that efforts were made to create a realistic and implementable budget, rather than an overly ambitious one, by focusing on new income streams and reducing unnecessary expenses without imposing new taxes.

Historical data reveals a significant gap between DSCC's announced budgets and actual expenditures. For instance, in FY2022-23, only 29.6% of the Tk 6,741.28 crore budget was implemented, and in FY2023-24, 37.7% of the Tk 6,751.56 crore budget was utilized. The average implementation rate over three fiscal years has been around 33%.

The allocation for cleanliness has been quadrupled to Tk 327 crore from the revised Tk 80.38 crore last year. However, Tk 180 crore of this is designated for the wages of irregular workers, rather than new vehicles, machinery, or waste management infrastructure.

Similarly, the health sector budget increased to Tk 121.66 crore from Tk 35.79 crore. Yet, Tk 55 crore is for irregular workers' wages and Tk 50.50 crore for mosquito control pesticides, accounting for approximately 87% of the total health allocation.

The substantial allocation for mosquito control is crucial, as surveys show high Aedes mosquito larva density in 63 out of 75 wards. The administrator emphasized the need for effective pesticide use, along with transparent reporting on its efficacy and results.

Revenue projections include Tk 400 crore from 'liability increase,' comprising Tk 200 crore from suspense accounts and Tk 200 crore from contractors' security deposits. These are not regular income sources from taxes, fees, or services.

A target of Tk 200 crore from road excavation fees is also ambitious, given that actual income from this sector was only Tk 10.70 crore in FY2024-25. This target relies heavily on a specific Dhaka WASA sewerage project, rather than regular revenue generation. The target for government and foreign aid-dependent development income is Tk 1,457.93 crore, nearly triple the actual receipt from the previous year.
